title: DROP INDEX
description: Learn how to remove indexes from tables using the DROP INDEX statement.

data.text: The DROP INDEX statement removes one or more indexes from the current database. Use the IF EXISTS option to avoid errors when dropping an index that may not exist.

data.title: DROP INDEX with IF EXISTS
data.content: Safely drops an index if it exists.
data.code:
DROP INDEX [IF EXISTS] index_name
ON table_name;

data.text: Note that the IF EXISTS option has been available since SQL Server 2016 (13.x). The DROP INDEX statement does not remove indexes created by PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraints — use ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT for those.

data.title: Drop one index
data.content: Removes the ix_cust_email index from the customers table.
data.code:
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_cust_email
ON sales.customers;

data.title: Drop multiple indexes
data.content: Removes multiple indexes from the same table in one statement.

data.title: DROP INDEX Key Points
points: Use DROP INDEX to remove non-clustered indexes from tables.
Always use IF EXISTS to avoid errors on non-existent indexes.
DROP INDEX cannot remove indexes created by PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraints.
You can drop multiple indexes in a single DROP INDEX statement.
